title: The Forgotten Salt
premise: Odile Ravensworth fled into the Salt Valley a decade ago, where the brine-choked air deadens magic and hides her from the storm-court that branded her a traitor. When she finds her own name and tonight's date inked in a century-old prophecy, she learns her soul was sold before her birth to the court beneath the mountain, and that the debt comes due at moonset. To reclaim it she must ally with Casimir, the prophecy's scribe trapped in undeath, and descend through courts of salt and shadow where every bargain costs more than it seems. In the end Odile chooses to shatter the debt-magic itself rather than rule it, freeing the mountain's enslaved souls at the price of her own powers—and choosing love and mortality over the immortality she could have seized.
about_author: Petra Halloran is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing obscure grimoires in coastal libraries. She writes fantasy about bargains, exile, and the people history forgets to record.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Establishes her quiet life as a salt-harvester in the magic-dead valley, her careful routines, and her friendship with the innkeeper Maren. The emotional beat is brittle contentment—she has built peace on top of fear, and we feel how hard she works not to remember why.

chapters.title: Ink Older Than Grief
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A peddler sells her a water-damaged book; inside, a prophecy written a century ago names her and tonight's date. The beat is vertigo: her invisibility was an illusion, her life a scheduled event. She burns the page, but the words reappear on her skin.

chapters.title: The Scribe Who Would Not Die
chapters.summary: Casimir's POV. Introduces the undead scribe who wrote the prophecy and has waited a hundred years for Odile, bound to witness but never intervene. His guilt and tenderness toward her complicate everything. Beat: reluctant alliance sealed by mutual need, not trust.

chapters.title: What the Mountain Holds
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Casimir reveals her parents sold her soul to the Undercourt to buy her exile and safety; the debt matures at moonset, three days hence. Beat: fury and betrayal—her whole protected life was a payment plan. She decides to go down and steal herself back.

chapters.title: The Tollgate of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The descent begins: a border market where travelers pay with memories. Odile trades her memory of home; Casimir secretly pays her toll himself. Beat: first taste of the mountain's cruelty and first crack in her armor toward him.

chapters.title: Court of Brine and Bone
chapters.summary: Casimir's POV. They reach the Undercourt, where the Salt Queen rules over souls kept as currency. Odile sees what power looks like when it wins completely. Beat: dread sharpened by fascination—the Queen offers Odile a place beside her instead of freedom.

chapters.title: A Bargain With Teeth
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. To reach her soul-vault, Odile accepts the Queen's wager: three trials, each demanding she sacrifice something she loves. She passes two by sacrificing her storm-calling and her memories of Casimir. Beat: grief disguised as strategy; love against duty begins to cost real blood.

chapters.title: The Third Trial
chapters.summary: Casimir's POV. The final trial demands Casimir's final death—he is the last thing she loves. He goes willingly; she refuses, breaking the trial's terms. Beat: climax of the heart. Her refusal cracks the debt-magic, revealing the Queen's own stolen soul at its core.

chapters.title: Moonset Over the Deep Court
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Climax. At moonset Odile shatters the soul-ledger rather than claim her soul alone, unbinding every enslaved spirit including the Queen's. The mountain convulses; they escape as the court collapses. Beat: triumph inseparable from loss—she is mortal now, powerless, and free.

chapters.title: Salt in the Wound, Light in the Air
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Resolution. Back in the valley, Odile rebuilds her life without magic or her traded memories, while Casimir, freed by the ledger's fall, ages like a man again. Maren returns her a keepsake that stirs what was lost. Beat: quiet hope—survival's price paid, love chosen anyway.
